### 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The dataset of 1,006 draws provides a comprehensive view of the distribution patterns in this lottery game. The most striking observation is the presence of hot and cold numbers, with some numbers appearing more frequently than others. The analysis reveals that certain numbers, such as 5, 14, and 43, have a higher frequency of appearance, while others, like 9 and 49, are relatively less frequent. The data also shows a consistent year-to-year pattern, with some numbers performing well across multiple years.

The distribution of even and odd numbers is relatively balanced, with a slight tilt towards even numbers. The analysis of consecutive number occurrences reveals that some numbers are more likely to appear in close proximity, while others are more dispersed. The winner pattern analysis shows that certain numbers are more likely to appear in winning draws, while others are less represented.

The temporal trends in the data reveal that some numbers are more consistent performers across years, while others experience fluctuations. The recent shifts in patterns are also observed, with some numbers experiencing a surge in frequency in recent years.

#### b) Pattern & Distribution Analysis

The analysis of even/odd and high/low balance reveals that the distribution is relatively balanced, with a slight tilt towards even numbers. The consecutive number occurrences reveal that some numbers, such as 14 and 43, are more likely to appear in close proximity, while others, like 9 and 49, are more dispersed.

#### c) Winner Pattern Analysis

The winner pattern analysis reveals that certain numbers, such as 1, 2, and 22, are more likely to appear in winning draws, while others, like 15 and 32, are less represented. This suggests that these numbers may have an advantage in winning draws.

#### d) Temporal Trends

The year-to-year consistency patterns reveal that some numbers, such as 8 and 2, are consistent performers across multiple years. The recent shifts in patterns are also observed, with some numbers experiencing a surge in frequency in recent years.
